record.paper_title: Solving the Integrated Bin Allocation and Collection Routing Problem for Municipal Solid Waste: a Benders Decomposition Approach
record.original_question: How can the integrated bin-allocation and collection-routing model for garbage-accumulation-point municipal solid waste systems be extended from a homogeneous fleet of collection vehicles to a heterogeneous fleet, including the small-capacity vans for spot operations already owned by Bahía Blanca?

evidence.quote: We consider an homogeneous fleet of vehicles.
We could also explore heterogeneous fleet of vehicles. Indeed, the city of Bahía Blanca already owns a fleet of vans of small capacity for spot operations.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Consider a municipal solid waste collection system based on garbage accumulation points (GAPs). Let $N=\{1,\dots,n\}$ be a set of candidate GAP locations in a road network modeled as a graph $G=(V,E)$ with travel costs/times $c_{ij}$ on each arc $(i,j)$. Each location $i\in N$ has a known waste-generation rate $w_i\ge 0$, and one must choose, for each open GAP, a bin configuration from a finite catalogue $\mathcal{B}$ of bins (each bin $b\in\mathcal{B}$ has capacity $Q_b$, installation cost $f_b$, and footprint constraints), such that the installed capacity covers the assigned demand within a chosen collection frequency. Households/users are assigned to open GAPs subject to a maximum walking-distance constraint.

In the homogeneous-fleet version, a fleet of $K$ identical collection vehicles, each of capacity $Q$ and depot $0$, must perform routes that visit every open GAP often enough to empty it before overflow, minimizing total installation plus routing cost.

Formulate and solve the analogous integrated bin-allocation and collection-routing optimization problem in the case of a heterogeneous fleet: assume there are vehicle types $t\in T$ with capacities $Q_t$, fixed/operating costs $F_t$, speed and accessibility parameters $\alpha_t$ (so that some street segments or GAPs may be reachable only by certain vehicle types), and a fixed available number $K_t$ of each type, including small-capacity vans suitable for spot operations. Specifically:

(a) Provide a mixed-integer programming formulation that simultaneously decides (i) which GAPs to open and which bin configuration to install at each, (ii) the assignment of users to GAPs, and (iii) a feasible set of routes assigned to vehicles of the heterogeneous fleet, minimizing total installation, fixed vehicle, and routing costs.

(b) Develop a Benders-decomposition-based exact or matheuristic solution method for this heterogeneous extension, characterizing the feasibility and optimality cuts induced by the heterogeneous capacity and accessibility constraints.

(c) Prove convergence/correctness of the proposed algorithm and analyze its computational performance compared with the homogeneous-fleet baseline.
artifact.status_search_result: No published follow-up addressing the heterogeneous-fleet extension of this integrated bin-allocation and collection-routing model with a Benders decomposition approach was located. The original work explicitly leaves this as future research, and standard heterogeneous-fleet VRP literature does not appear to incorporate the joint bin-allocation decision considered here. Status is therefore unknown.

status_evidence.title: Solving the Integrated Bin Allocation and Collection Routing Problem (arXiv abstract)
status_evidence.snippet: The paper assumes a homogeneous fleet and lists heterogeneous-fleet extension as future work.
status_evidence.claim: The heterogeneous-fleet extension is identified as an open future-research direction by the original modelers.
